name: Sales call tracker - WhatsApp to Sheets

parameters.content:
## 1 · Set the goal, every weekday at 08:30
Reads the **Roster** tab, keeps the people marked active, and tells each one what today's target is. Nobody is asked anything yet — they can report whenever they like.

The row is written to the **Log** tab straight away with `status = goal_set` and an empty `calls` cell. That empty cell is what lane 1b looks for at the end of the day, and what makes a *silent* day visible in the report — a blank is not a zero.

`key` (`date|phone`) is built here and rebuilt by lanes 1b and 2, so everything that happens today updates this one row.

## 1b · Nudge the quiet ones, 16:30
Reads the **Log**, keeps today's rows whose `calls` cell is still empty, and reminds only those people. Anyone who already reported hears nothing.

**Why the fork.** WhatsApp only allows free-form text within 24 hours of the person's own last message. Inside that window Claude writes a nudge from their week so far; outside it the message legally has to be an approved template, so it is one. The window state is computed in **Who still owes a number**, from the log's own reply timestamps.

**Write the nudge** continues on error, so a missing Anthropic credential lands on the template path rather than skipping the nudge.

messageValues.message: You write one-line WhatsApp nudges for a sales coach. Warm and specific, at most 25 words, no emoji, no greeting boilerplate. Use only the numbers you are given - never invent one. Always end by asking how many calls they made today. Reply with the message text only.

assignments.name: message
assignments.value: ={{ ($json.text || '').trim().replace(/^["']|["']$/g, '').slice(0, 900) || ('Hi ' + $('Who still owes a number').item.json.name + " - how many calls did " + 'you get done today?') }}

parameters.content:
## 2 · Collect the reply
Cheap path first: a bare number, "all" or "none" is parsed in code and costs nothing. Only the tail — *"did 6, two no-shows"* — reaches the model.

**Read it with Claude** is set to *continue using error output*, so a missing Anthropic credential degrades to "reply with a plain number" instead of dropping the answer.

The upsert matches on `key`, so a reply lands on the row this morning's nudge created.

attributes.name: calls
attributes.description: =Number of sales calls the person says they completed today. Their daily target is {{ $json.target }}; if they say they did all of them, that is the number. Count only calls already made — ignore calls they plan to make later. Leave empty if no count can be determined from the message.

attributes.name: note
attributes.description: Anything the person said about why, in at most six words (for example 'two no-shows' or 'sick'). Empty if they gave no reason.

options.systemPromptTemplate: You are reading a sales rep's WhatsApp reply to "how many calls did you make today?". Extract only what the message actually states. Do not guess a number.

parameters.textBody: =Logged {{ Number($('Have a number?').item.json.calls) }}/{{ $('Have a number?').item.json.target }} for {{ $('Have a number?').item.json.weekday }} {{ $('Have a number?').item.json.date }}. {{ Number($('Have a number?').item.json.calls) >= Number($('Have a number?').item.json.target) ? 'Target hit.' : (Number($('Have a number?').item.json.target) - Number($('Have a number?').item.json.calls)) + ' short of target.' }}
=Sorry, I couldn't read a number out of that. How many sales calls did you get done today? Just the number is fine (0-{{ $('Match rep & parse reply').item.json.target }}).

parameters.content:
## 3 · Graph it, Fridays at 17:00
Two surfaces, two jobs. The **Weekly** tab gets the per-day detail, so the client can pivot and chart it in the spreadsheet they already live in. WhatsApp gets a single progress-to-goal bar, which is the only shape that still reads on a phone as the roster grows.

The chart is a Chart.js config rendered by QuickChart — the same config drops into a web dashboard later without rewriting the aggregation.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ chart: $json.chart, width: 820, height: $json.height, backgroundColor: 'white', devicePixelRatio: 2, format: 'png' }) }}

nodes.name: Send the chart to the coach

main.node: Send the chart to the coach
